selection.assessment: The broad Liberal Arts and Sciences response owns all seven direct programme interests and implements the selected film-and-television specialization while preserving humanities, science and social-science breadth. Two further interest clusters—environmental sustainability and digital society/AI—each support coherent, mechanically feasible UCR programmes that differ by at least 30 EC from every other alternative. Production stops because three UCR alternatives is the permitted maximum.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized Liberal Arts and Sciences target does not choose among more than forty formal main directions. The current prospective-student list orders Film- en televisiewetenschap first, so that specialization is selected by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. The minimum formal 67.5-EC main-direction size is instantiated and the remaining 52.5 EC is retained as open profiling space.

comparator.name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 programme-specific OER defines a 180-EC programme with 60 EC of General Education, a main direction of 67.5–105 EC and the balance as profiling space. General Education comprises four compulsory 7.5-EC LAS courses and 30 EC of electives split equally across the two science groups outside the chosen main direction. The generic target does not choose among the formal main directions, so the first current direction on the prospective-student list, Film- en televisiewetenschap (group A), is selected by official-order tie-break. A minimum-size 67.5-EC main direction is instantiated, including its required 7.5-EC final work, leaving 52.5 EC of open profiling space. The programme also requires a zero-credit portfolio, which is recorded here but does not alter the 180-EC total.

alternatives.label: Interdisciplinary Media, Society & Science
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum uses media and communication as its coherent specialization while maintaining substantial social-science, behavioural, quantitative and scientific breadth, accurately reflecting its liberal-arts-and-sciences structure.
alternatives.concept: A broad interdisciplinary liberal arts and sciences programme organised around media and communication, integrating cultural analysis with sociology, politics, psychology, economics, data and research methods.
progression: Six fixed four-course semesters in 2026–29; PPD is in Year 1, advanced media, communication and social-science work follows introductory study, and official workbook term availability and formal prerequisites were verified.

alternatives.label: Sustainability, Environment & Public Change
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum connects environmental and delta science with economics, law, politics, sociology, data and communication, so the label names both its scientific centre and public-change dimension.
alternatives.concept: An interdisciplinary sustainability route combining environmental systems and climate adaptation with economics, governance, law, policy, sociology, data and public communication.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces the closest programme’s media-specialist and organisational sequence with sustained environmental science, sustainability, delta, economics, law and public-policy study; substantially more than four courses change in both directions.
progression: Six fixed four-course semesters in 2026–29; PPD is in Year 1, gateway and introductory environmental courses precede advanced environmental and delta work, and official workbook term availability and formal prerequisites were verified.

alternatives.label: Digital Society, AI & Media Culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum joins a substantial AI and computation sequence to sustained media, communication and social analysis, directly supporting a digital-society and media-culture label.
alternatives.concept: An interdisciplinary digital-society route combining artificial intelligence, programming, machine learning and data with media studies, communication, cultural analysis and social inquiry.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces much of the closest programme’s social-science, behavioural and business sequence with programming, logic, machine learning, deep learning, intelligent systems, algorithms and mathematics while retaining a coherent media strand; it also differs from the sustainability route by well over four courses in both directions.
progression: Six fixed four-course semesters in 2026–29; PPD is in Year 1, programming and mathematical foundations precede advanced AI, algorithms and media work, and official workbook term availability and formal prerequisites were verified.

notes.text: Utrecht LAS combines a compulsory interdisciplinary core with a formally approved main direction, two General Education fields, profiling space, a programme thesis and a separate main-direction final work. UCR is itself a liberal arts and sciences college and can construct close interdisciplinary equivalents, but it does not reproduce Utrecht’s exact LAS core, approval structure or double-final-work requirement.
